paragraphs.text: We report methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) perovskite solar cells (PSCs) that reach a certified power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.1% under 1-sun AM1.5G illumination at initial scan.
Perovskite solar cells have advanced rapidly, yet long-term operational stability remains the key barrier to commercialization.
Devices were fabricated on fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) glass substrates with a compact TiO2 electron transport layer deposited by spray pyrolysis.
The MAPbI3 absorber was deposited by a one-step spin-coating method, followed by spiro-OMeTAD as the hole transport layer and a gold electrode.
X-ray diffraction (XRD) confirmed a phase-pure tetragonal MAPbI3 film with no detectable PbI2 residue.
The champion device delivered a PCE of 21.1% with an open-circuit voltage of 1.12 V and a fill factor of 0.80 under 1-sun illumination.
Encapsulated devices retained 95% of their initial PCE after 200 h of shelf storage in the dark.
The hysteresis index was not measured in this study.
We attribute the high initial efficiency to the compact TiO2 layer, which suppresses interfacial recombination.
These results show that compact TiO2 based PSCs can combine high initial PCE with good shelf stability.
Current density-voltage curves were recorded with a masked aperture of 0.09 cm2.

paragraphs.text: We examine the damp-heat stability of MAPbI3 perovskite solar cells and find that encapsulated devices retain a PCE of 18.7% after 500 h of aging at 85 °C and 85% relative humidity.
Initial efficiencies above 21% have been reported for MAPbI3 cells, but their stability under damp-heat stress is rarely quantified.
MAPbI3 films were prepared by sequential deposition on mesoporous TiO2 scaffolds infiltrated with the perovskite precursor.
The hole transport material was 2,2',7,7'-tetrakis(N,N-di-p-methoxyphenylamino)-9,9'-spirobifluorene (spiro-OMeTAD), doped with Li-TFSI.
Devices were encapsulated with a glass-glass lamination using a UV-curable epoxy edge seal.
The damp-heat protocol held devices at 85 °C and 85% relative humidity (RH) without illumination.
Unencapsulated devices failed completely within 200 h, whereas the encapsulated MAPbI3 device retained a PCE of 18.7% after 500 h of damp-heat aging, corresponding to 89% of its initial value.
XRD patterns recorded after aging show the emergence of PbI2 peaks, indicating partial decomposition of the MAPbI3 absorber.
We hypothesize that the mesoporous TiO2 scaffold accelerates moisture ingress compared with compact layers.
Glass-glass encapsulation improves the damp-heat stability of MAPbI3 devices.
PCE was tracked every 24 h under open-circuit conditions in the dark between aging intervals.
